content.user_title: Improve Code Changes with Development Guidance
content.value_statement: Code edits can drift from project style or miss important edge cases. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through planning, implementation, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Guides codebase exploration with fd, rg, and standard shell tools.
Promotes readable, maintainable code and simple working solutions.
Requires explicit approval before non-trivial implementation plans.
Encourages git safety before repository initialization or branch changes.
Directs Python work to import and circular dependency guidance.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts or automated fixes.
Provides broad process guidance, not full language documentation.
Depends on the host AI tool to apply repository changes correctly.
Does not replace project tests or human code review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Code Change
use_cases.description: Structure a non-trivial implementation with clarifying questions, proposed answers, and an approval checkpoint.

use_cases.title: Refactor Existing Code
use_cases.description: Improve maintainability while preserving local style, documenting intent, and checking edge cases.

use_cases.title: Review Python Structure
use_cases.description: Use the Python reference to spot import placement issues and circular dependency patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the develop skill to inspect this project and summarize its main structure, likely entry points, and verification commands.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the develop skill to plan this feature: [feature]. Ask clarifying questions with proposed answers before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the develop skill to refactor [module] for readability while matching existing style and preserving behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Risky Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the develop skill to create a staged plan for [large change], including edge cases, git safety checks, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Improve a failing test workflow in a small service.
output: A concise plan with clarifying questions and proposed answers.
A focused implementation path that follows existing project style.
Verification steps that include the relevant test command.

output_examples.input: Refactor a Python module with circular import pressure.
output: A recommendation to move shared definitions into a separate module.
A warning against hiding the issue with type-checking guards.
A final check that imports remain at the top of the file.

best_practices: Share the target files, expected behavior, and test command before implementation.
Use the planning step for broad changes and approve the plan before edits start.
Ask for verification results after file edits.
anti_patterns: Use it as a replacement for project-specific coding standards.
Skip tests because the skill recommends simple solutions.
Apply broad rewrites when targeted edits would solve the issue.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI coding tools explore codebases, plan changes, edit carefully, and verify results.

faq.question: Does it run commands by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance to the host AI tool, which controls any command execution.

faq.question: Can it handle Python projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a short Python reference for import placement and circular dependency cleanup.

faq.question: Is it only for large projects?
faq.answer: No. It can guide small fixes, focused refactors, and larger planned changes.

faq.question: Does it replace testing?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly encourages verification after edits and does not replace project tests.

faq.question: Which tools support it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
